tools.name: Anticyclotomic theta functional-equation parity screen
tools.abstraction: For a nonzero one-variable Iwasawa element whose inversion functional equation has sign epsilon and a multiplicative group-like factor of augmentation one, pass to the first nonzero augmentation-graded piece: inversion contributes (-1)^r, so the vanishing-order parity must match epsilon when 2 is invertible.
preconditions: one-variable Iwasawa algebra Lambda=O[[Gamma]] with Gamma isomorphic to Z_p and augmentation ideal J
Theta is nonzero with finite r=ord_J Theta
the involution is induced by gamma -> gamma^{-1}
Theta^* = epsilon * Theta * u with epsilon in {+1,-1} and u congruent to 1 modulo J
structural_signature: exact vanishing order is measured in powers of the augmentation ideal
a functional equation relates inversion of the same element to itself times a sign and augmentation-one unit
the first graded piece is torsion-free enough that multiplication by 2 cannot kill a nonzero leading class
tools.operation: Take the nonzero class of Theta in J^r/J^(r+1). Replace the inversion by multiplication by (-1)^r on the graded piece and replace u by 1. Conclude (-1)^r=epsilon. In the BSD source instantiation epsilon=+1, hence r is even; combine separately with source-proved r>0.
guaranteed_effects: rules out the parity opposite to the functional-equation sign within the registered algebraic scope
for the Castella-Hsieh trivial-character theta element with root sign +1 and good p>3, upgrades r>0 to r>=2
non_guarantees: does not bound r from above
does not prove Mordell-Weil rank, Selmer dimension, Sha finiteness, regulator nonvanishing or any BSD leading-term identity
does not apply when the functional-equation normalization/sign or augmentation-one factor is not established
validation_obligations: bind the exact functional equation and its normalization to the same theta element whose augmentation order is measured
verify the group-like/unit factor has augmentation one
verify 2 is invertible and Theta is nonzero
separate parity from exact-order and arithmetic-rank conclusions
rerun the sign-minus-one, p=2 and zero-element hostile controls before reuse in a changed context
evidence_pointers: Castella-Hsieh, Forum Math. Sigma 10 (2022), Section 5.3, DOI 10.1017/fms.2021.85
